You'll note that when it comes to university time, rich Chinese parents are still falling over themselves to put their kids in Western universities, not the other way around.

You get two things at universities: networking and to a lesser extent learning from people with high-value (in western money) experience. There's a lot of bureaucratic inertia behind still trying to hire people with an ivy on their resume, especially on non-technical tracks, so it's well founded.

Would Chinese-style education work on British kids?

If only.

I don't think you'd actually want to.

While they're doing an incredible job of instilling fact regurgitation and mechanical operations into the children, it seems something isn't clicking when it comes time for those kids to enter the real world and convert that knowledge into something greater. China, a country with a population of more than a billion than than the US, has only had 12 Nobel laureates and only 8 in the sciences. This isn't to say Chinese are not publishing in western journals - they are in mass. It's just that the research they're producing is not being deemed particularly ground breaking.

Ultimately I think just looking at the standardized test scores and looking to emulate it is myopic. We should look at the ends of education which most assuredly not a standardized test. And in that ends the Chinese education system does not seem to be producing the sort of student you would desire.

No. East-Asian-style educations is fucking retarded. They basically abuse their kids by cramming "education" down their throats from as young as 3 years old until they're out of college.
